CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 8, 2021 -4:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 4:06 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Madison.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Cou ncilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  ROSE BOWL OPERATING COMPANY (RBOC) AT-A-GLANCE:
  PRESENTATION OF FIVE-YEAR PROFORMA AND REVENUE
  OPPORTUNITIES PLAN
.....,...."'
  Recommendation: This presentation is for information only; no
  action is required at this time.

  FISCAL YEAR 2022 OPERATING BUDGET PRESENTATION
  AND REVIEW OF THE ROSE BOWL OPERATING COMPANY
  Recommendation: This presentation is for information only; no
  action is required at this time.

  The above two items were discussed concurrently.

  Councilmember Williams disclosed that she is a board member of
  Wescom Credit Union, which is a sponsor of the Rose Bowl
  Stadium, but stated that she does not view her participation in the
  RBOC budget review item as a conflict of interest.

  Mayor Gordo provided introductory comments on the challenges
  related to the Rose Bowl Stadium and the City's responsibilities. He
  stated that he is going to assign an ad hoc committee to work with
  the Rose Bowl Operating Company (RBOC) and the Pasadena
  Center Operating Company (PCOC) to help focus on and vet the
  budget issues/details, and provide guidance to the City Council.

  Council Minutes  06/08/2021
   Steve Haderlein, President of the Rose Bowl Operating Company
  (RBOC), provided introductory comments, spoke on the highly
  variable Fiscal Year 2022 RBOC budget; and responded to
  questions.

  Darryl Dunn, Chief Executive Officer at the Rose Bowl Stadium,
  provided introductory comments, and Dan Barrett, Executive Vice
  President with CAAICON (RBOC's consultant), presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on RBOC 's financial status, as well as
  revenue opportunities and analysis, with both responding to
  questions.

  Councilmember Madison supported serious City Council
  consideration regarding the potential opportunities/projects
  proposed by RBOC's consultants; and spoke in favor of the City's
  continued support of the RBOC, highlighted by the New Year's Day
  benefits that are derived from the Rose Bowl Stadium.

  Vice Mayor Wilson encouraged RBOC staff to reduce the number
  of potential revenue opportunities/projects to focus on 20-25 such
  events, considering the timeline, impacts to the surrounding area,
  and likelihood of meeting revenue targets. He also asked RBOC
  staff to consider re-conceptualizing the Arroyo Seco area and
  expanding opportunities for the entire area from a strategic position.

  Mayor Gordo voiced support for RBOC staff to re-conceptualize the
  Arroyo Seco area and beyond , taking into consideration
  Pasadena's next evolution as it pertains to sports, arts,
  entertainment, conventions, and hospitality, as well as doing so in
  a responsible manner. He also spoke on the need to include
  Brookside Golf Club and the Pasadena Center Operating Company
  (PCOC) as part of the discussion when analyzing Pasadena's next
  evolution.

  Councilmember Williams spoke in favor of reducing the number of
  potential opportunities/projects to a feasible number. She
  requested the following:

  •  City staff to engage a bond counsel and calculation to
  determine what might be done in regards to the Rose Bowl
  debt service and Build America Bonds;
  •  Staff to determine if the extraordinary redemption is
  applicable, and if there is an option, to refund a portion of
  the debt on a tax exempt basis;
  •  She suggested that the Legislative Policy Committee work
  with the City's lobbyist to follow up on the Build America
  Bonds (BAB) legislation as part of an infrastructure bill and
  to determine if it is possible through legislation to reinstate
  35% IRS subsidy;

Council Minutes  2  06/08/2021
   •  She also suggested that the Finance Committee review the
  debt policy for the City to determine if it should be amended
  to provide refunds;
  •  She asked staff to provide information on RBOC 's annual
--  contribution to CalPERS and their unfunded accrued
  liability.

  Matt Hawkesworth, Director of Finance, stated that he would
  provide the additional requested information; noted staff's current
  engagement with bond counsel related to extraordinary measures:
  and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need for RBOC to
  reimagine the Arroyo Seco from La Casita Del Arroyo up north to
  the Devils Gate Reservoir. He suggested that a comprehensive
  review of the area is undertaken; and incorporate the surrounding
  neighborhoods, as well as Councilmembers Hampton and Madison,
  into the process. Councilmember Kennedy suggested that the City
  seek the assistance of Mr. Dickran Tevrizian and Jim Ellis, or
  someone similar, to assist in reimaging the Arroyo Seco and meet
  with the RBOC to attract investment. He spoke on the need to
  address and improve the fan experience at the Rose Bowl Stadium;
  and to consider the Latino/Latinx community in terms of concerts.
  In addition, he requested information on RBOC, and that City staff
  consider possible structural changes in terms of the RBOC and City
  (i.e. continuing as an operating company, transitioning into the City
  governmental structure under the purview of the City Manager,
  etc.); and information on what is the approximate investment
  required related strictly to infrastructure.

  Nina Chomsky, representing the Linda Vista-Annandale
  Association, advocated for the continued protection and
  security of the surrounding neighborhoods of the Rose Bowl
  Stadium; and balance the naturalization efforts and the needs
  of the RBOC in the Arroyo Seco. She personally advocated for
  the City to refinance the BAB agreement.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that correspondence was
  received in support of the Rose Bowl Operating Company, and/or
  expressed concerns with their financial challenges, which were
  distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the
  public record .

  Councilmember Hampton spoke on the need for RBOC, PCOC and
  the newly appointed ad hoc committee to be fully engaged in the
  discussion on the ideas related to the Arroyo Seco and surrounding
  areas, including the possible installation of an ice skating rink. He
  echoed comments related to the need to continue the dialogue
  between the Rose Bowl Stadium and surrounding neighborhoods.

  Council Minutes  3  06/08/2021
   Following discussion, Mr. Haderlein stated that the RBOC staff will
  present a second analysis and an update on their budget to the City
  Council in approximately 4 -5 months.

  Mr. Dunn, provided information on upcoming events at the Rose
  Bowl Stadium.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus of
  the City Council, the information was received and filed.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjourned at 6:24 p.m.

  Victor M. Gordo, Mayor
  City of Pasadena
